declaration.description: Message registry for SYS onboard status, button eventing and policy-bound internal text storage.

message_contract.context: Legacy int msgId carries a 32-bit context rendered as uppercase X8.

resource_contract.open: OPEN is the mandatory loosely decoupled attach boundary. The platform entry resolves Deployment HAL references and supplies target configuration at runtime; the agile module contains no compiler-hardcoded target values.
resource_contract.close: CLOSE drives safe state, releases resources and is idempotent.
resource_contract.info: INFO is valid while open or closed.

LOOPBACK.behavior: Publish ECHO with LOOPBACK_TEST and same context.

OPEN.rule: Validate and attach the configuration resolved from the selected HAL NEO binding. Populate runtime fields only after successful acquisition; driver null is the authoritative closed state.

CLOSE.rule: Stop activity, set pixels OFF, dispose the pixel driver, drive optional power inactive and close only the optional power pin. Retain the SYS module controller. Preserve last successful OPEN configuration; reset hardware/interaction state only.

SET.rule: Apply immediately to the onboard status indicator; last physical write wins.

BLINK.execution: Synchronous best-effort color/sleep/OFF/sleep repetitions; remain OFF; no EmitEvent, sequence ownership or reservation.

INFO.rule: Defaults apply before the first successful OPEN. Successful new OPEN atomically commits the validated binding; failed OPEN and OPEN-already preserve the last successful binding. CLOSE releases hardware but retains this binding; repeated CLOSE is idempotent. INFO is available open or closed; opened derives only from the nullable hardware object. Reopening still requires explicit OPEN arguments; no new implicit OPEN form.

color_contract.state: Color is converted for the immediate platform write and is not retained for GET.

OPEN.rule: Attach the HAL-resolved onboard LED at runtime; retain no compiler-hardcoded target pin or polarity.

CLOSE.rule: Drive the LED inactive, close only its runtime pin and retain the SYS module controller. Preserve last successful OPEN configuration; reset hardware/interaction state only.

TOGGLE.rule: Toggle the physical pin without retaining shadow state.

INFO.rule: Defaults apply before the first successful OPEN. Successful new OPEN atomically commits the validated binding; failed OPEN and OPEN-already preserve the last successful binding. CLOSE releases hardware but retains this binding; repeated CLOSE is idempotent. INFO is available open or closed; opened derives only from the nullable hardware object. Reopening still requires explicit OPEN arguments; no new implicit OPEN form.

LED.selection_rule: This package binds one onboard LED, so the target is implicit and no index is accepted.

CLOSE.rule: Disable delivery, detach named Press and Holding callbacks and dispose GpioButton with shouldDispose=false so its pin is released. Retain the SYS module controller and all subscriptions; do not close the button pin twice. Preserve last successful OPEN configuration; reset hardware/interaction state only.

CLOSE releases hardware but retains this binding; repeated CLOSE is idempotent. INFO is available open or closed; opened derives only from the nullable hardware object. Reopening still requires explicit OPEN arguments; no new implicit OPEN form.
INFO.mode_encoding: Selected nanoFramework PinMode.ToString() representation; the tested firmware renders InputPullUp as 2. This patch does not introduce normalized enum-name output.

events.counter_contract: Positive decimal count of accepted Press callbacks since successful OPEN; same counter for short and holding-related PRESS.
events.open_context_contract: args[1] is ctx + successful new BUTTON OPEN command msgId formatted uppercase X8, e.g. ctx08000005. This is lifecycle provenance, not event ctx or authentication. Repeated OPEN-already retains the original open ctx. CLOSE clears it. Physical interaction ctx allocation/preservation remains unchanged.
Single argument ctx + successful OPEN command msgId formatted X8. Event ctx remains the interaction context and must not be replaced by the marker.

FLASH.condition: Generated only when Deployment enables and binds SYS FLASH.

CREATE.visibility: Generated PlatformPostInit operation; not a runtime scope OPEN.
CREATE.selection: Only missing Deployment-declared RD roots are supplied. Omit CREATE when all RD roots already exist.
CREATE.behavior: Create requested root directories idempotently; preserve existing roots and all content; create no files, nested content or RW roots; leave FLASH closed.
CREATE.emits: /FLASH/CREATE once only when at least one root was created

OPEN.initial_binding: The generated activation may append the Deployment binding on the first OPEN only; public callers cannot replace it.
OPEN.emits: /FLASH/OPEN only on the closed-to-open transition; the already-open response emits no event

CLOSE.emits: /FLASH/CLOSE only on the open-to-closed transition; the already-closed response emits no event

INFO.accounting: RW usedBytes is aggregate UTF-8 file payload length inside only that logical scope; availableBytes=max(0,quotaBytes-usedBytes). RD has no quota accounting. Physical drive used/free is not part of this contract.

LDIR.behavior: Return only descendant directories recursively from the scope root or one existing selected level. Do not return the selected level itself, files or physical paths. Fixed page size is 16; next=-1 ends traversal.

LIST.behavior: Return only files directly inside exactly one existing logical pathscope. Never return directories and never recurse. Fixed page size is 16; next=-1 ends traversal.

policy.scope_selector: Logical Deployment scope name, never a physical path.
policy.mode: RD allows READ/EXISTS; RW also allows WRITE/DELETE.
policy.quota: Each RW scope enforces max_size_bytes aggregate encoded bytes.
policy.content: Text files only; current AT transport accepts one single-line payload and preserves a quoted comma-containing final payload.
policy.discovery: LDIR travels the directory hierarchy; LIST returns files in one exact pathscope. Both use deterministic ordinal ordering, offset paging with fixed page size 16, hide physical paths and emit no event.
policy.quota_accounting: For RW scopes, count aggregate UTF-8 payload bytes only within that scope. Scope available bytes is quota minus counted payload bytes. Do not report physical drive free space.
policy.provisioning: CREATE is deployment-only, consumes only RD logical-name/path pairs from the metadata connector, preserves existing content and does not open FLASH or lock the runtime policy.

OPEN.argument_counts: Including OPEN operation: 3 or 4 one-shot; 5 periodic. No other count.
OPEN.period_validation: When present, periodMs is decimal digits 1..2147483647 inclusive (leading zero digits accepted); empty, zero, negative, nondecimal, hexadecimal or overflow returns ERANGE. Validate count, ID, delay, tag and period before mutation/duplicate-already; errors retain all prior state. Keep existing ID/delay/tag validation.
OPEN.semantics: Omission selects existing one-shot. A supplied valid period configures periodic TMR without starting. Empty tag must retain positional field. Duplicate valid OPEN returns already with no configuration changes.

START.semantics: Existing optional delay updates first delay only. Active periodic returns already; cancelled periodic with an old delivery in flight returns EBUSY. periodMs retained.

RESTART.semantics: Reset interval and update optional checkpoint state; omitted fields retained. START/RESTART WDG responses use their requested operation, not tmr,wdg. Periodic resets first-delay sequence and preserves periodMs; during delivery EBUSY with no mutation.

CLOSE.periodic: During committed periodic delivery invalidate/remove logically immediately; shared-table closing tombstone reserves ID and capacity until completion. OPEN of that same ID before completion returns EBUSY; no new table. CLOSE,* count counts newly closed objects only; tombstones not double-counted.

INFO.periodic_detail: Existing ordered detail fields followed by ,mode=PERIODIC,periodMs=<n>,delivering=<bool>. type=TMR. remainingMs follows module periodic.remaining; a transient close tombstone reports state=closed and remainingMs=0. Legacy details unchanged.

LIST.names: Same summary; [<id>|...] for active entries only.
LIST.all: All retained entries including idle/expired; same summary and row format.
LIST.ordering: Case-sensitive ordinal ID order; [] valid. Default LIST hides standby entries.
LIST.periodic_row: <id>,<state>,<delayMs>,PERIODIC,<periodMs>; legacy one-shot/WDG rows stay <id>,<state>,<delayMs>. NAMES stays ID-only. Existing order/summary/selectors retained. Closing periodic tombstones appear only in ALL and count in poolCount until delivery finishes.

WDG.argument_counts: Including WDG operation: 4, 5 or 7. Six is EARGS. To bind correlation with an empty tag, pass empty tag position explicitly.
WDG.validation: Validate every argument before mutation. Consumer and id retain their existing exact endpoint/ID rules. Tag unchanged. expectedReply is one case-sensitive text argument, without comma, CR/LF or control characters. action is 1..64 ASCII letters/digits/_/- when enabled. expectedReply/action must both be empty or both nonempty; one alone is ECORRELATION.
WDG.atomicity: Success includes configuration of all metadata, managed subscription and arm. Internal helper overloads must not add capabilities absent from command args.

CANCEL.periodic: May stop periodic during delivery; old committed delivery finishes, future commitments/rearming prevented. Configuration retained; repeated idle CANCEL returns already.

WDG_CONFIRM.context: supervisedCtx accepts decimal or 0x-prefixed hexadecimal in 0..0x7FFFFFFF, preserving complete 32-bit supported runtime ctx. Do not apply the external WiFiAgent24-bit envelope limit to this payload argument.
WDG_CONFIRM.validation: Malformed ID/consumer/action/context/text or argument shape is an error; no mutation. Zero supervisedCtx has no correlation and is ignored, never auto-allocated.
WDG_CONFIRM.reason_selection: For a well-formed command: missing/non-WDG/idle/delivering -> not_pending; active at/past deadline -> expired; empty binding -> not_correlated; then ctx,consumer,action,reply mismatches in that order. Expired state may report expired; reason never authorizes action.
WDG_CONFIRM.errors: Existing EARGS/EID/ERANGE/EPLATFORM plus ECONSUMER/EACTION/EREPLY for malformed fields. Platform stop failure is EPLATFORM, not accepted.
WDG_CONFIRM.effects: Only accepted may stop/consume the matched WDG and reconcile its route. Ignored does not emit an event, alter state/deadline, remove a route, or affect unrelated entries.
WDG_CONFIRM.caller_rule: Parse explicit accepted result before application action. Generic +OK/ResultOk success is not a confirmation. Response uses commandCtx, not supervisedCtx.

payload_semantics.PER: count=1,2,... for committed expirations of current run; includes no-subscriber expirations; skipped scheduled slots do not increment
payload_semantics.reset: Successful START/RESTART and allocation/pool reuse reset ExpirationCount to zero; active START-already and duplicate OPEN retain state
payload_semantics.snapshot: Increment and capture under timerSync at commitment, before delivery outside the lock; committed event values remain independent of later control operations
payload_semantics.scope: Event payload only; existing INFO mode=PERIODIC and LIST PERIODIC strings remain unchanged

events.compatibility: First two positions unchanged; exact arity/payload consumers must account for two appended fields. WDG topic/payload unchanged.

errors.ERANGE: Invalid delay or supplied period outside positive decimal Int32 range
errors.ELIMIT: Configured capacity occupied with no reclaimable standby entry
errors.EPLATFORM: Timer allocation/Change failure; preserve consistent state
errors.EBUSY: Expiry delivery already committed, or active WDG consumer change; periodic RESTART or cancelled START during delivery, and OPEN on a still-closing periodic ID. Periodic active START returns already and periodic CANCEL/CLOSE remain permitted during delivery.
errors.ESUB: Managed subscription setup failed; trace original error
errors.ESUBOWNED: Foreign exact WDG PUSH route exists

TMR.event_rule: Only expiration emits TMR/WDG event. WDG and WDG_CONFIRM are synchronous commands; WDG_CONFIRM returns accepted/ignored/error, never invokes application action. Periodic repeats the same /TMR/EXPIRED payload/context under the approved no-overlap, fixed-cadence, skip-missed-slots policy. No subscriber is needed to continue scheduling.

endpoint_model.registry: business_commands is the dispatch endpoint registry; each entry declares kind.
endpoint_model.indices: Zero-based comma fields after AT+PUB=: direct command at [1], resource at [1], context at [2], resource command at [3]. Handler-local resource command is args[0].
endpoint_model.compatibility: Keep all existing wire syntax, response/event semantics, registry paths and handler delegate signatures unchanged. Periodic OPEN and periodic-only INFO/LIST fields extend the baseline; all legacy shapes remain unchanged.

producer.protocol: AT+PUB is an optional producer adapter and is not part of SYS business semantics.

validation.handler_rule: Register ECHO, INFO and LOOPBACK once, then register only SYS resources enabled by Deployment. NEO, LED, BUTTON and FLASH remain separate handlers.
validation.inherited_rule: Do not regenerate inherited Level 0 commands.
validation.context_rule: Every response and separately declared module event preserves incoming non-zero context.
validation.resource_rule: NEO and LED reuse OPEN/CLOSE/INFO and are synchronous push-only outputs. BUTTON reuses the lifecycle pattern but emits callback-driven events. Resources own pins, callbacks and drivers; the retained SYS module controller survives every CLOSE and failed-OPEN rollback. FLASH is policy-bound text storage and emits OPEN/CLOSE/WRITE/DELETE only after successful state change.
validation.scope_rule: Do not generate another planned SYS subsystem before its later contract exists.
lifecycle_isolation_checks: BUTTON CLOSE -> BUTTON INFO reports closed -> repeated BUTTON CLOSE returns already -> BUTTON OPEN succeeds -> PRESS and HOLDING callbacks work.
LED BLINK and NEO operations remain functional after BUTTON CLOSE.
LED CLOSE and OPEN do not change BUTTON, NEO or LORA behavior.
Failed OPEN rollback releases only resources acquired by that OPEN and permits a later valid OPEN.
Subscriptions survive resource CLOSE and OPEN cycles.
Use /BUTTON/** for a recursive SUBLIST selector that includes PRESS and both HOLDING child topics.
flash_checks: On first boot or after mass erase, PlatformPostInit sends CREATE only for missing RD scope roots; SYS creates the roots, leaves FLASH closed and emits/delivers one /FLASH/CREATE containing only created logical scope names.
On reboot or ordinary firmware reflash, existing RD roots and all existing content are preserved; CREATE is omitted and PlatformPostInit continues.
OPEN emits and delivers /FLASH/OPEN with compact Deployment-ordered scope descriptors and no physical used/free accounting.
CLOSE emits and delivers /FLASH/CLOSE with no arguments and preserves subscriptions.
General INFO returns opened state and compact scopes; INFO,<scope> returns RD policy or RW quota, logical used payload bytes and available quota without physical drive free-space claims.
WRITE with a comma-containing text payload preserves the complete payload and emits/delivers /FLASH/WRITE only after success.
READ and EXISTS return data and emit no FLASH event.
CLOSE emits/delivers /FLASH/CLOSE and preserves subscriptions; OPEN reuses the locked policy and emits/delivers /FLASH/OPEN.
RD mutation returns EREADONLY; invalid or escaping path returns EPATH; unknown scope returns ESCOPE; projected quota overflow returns EQUOTA without a success event.
recursive=false rejects descendant paths and recursive=true permits them.
LDIR returns only logical descendant directories from the root or selected existing level, hides physical paths, pages at 16 and emits no event.
LIST returns only direct files from one exact existing logical pathscope, never returns directories or recurses, pages at 16 and emits no event.
The data scope permits recursive RW navigation and mutation while enforcing its aggregate 65536-byte quota.
press_counter_checks: First three PRESS events contain 1,2,3; CLOSE/OPEN resets the next PRESS to 1; shared context logic remains unchanged.
validation.tmr_rule: Current focused integration acceptance: device/tests/FoundationPatchIntegrationAcceptance.md. Baseline periodic acceptance remains historical scope, not a new full-regression request.
